items.summary: The group said that it is exploring the use of artificial intelligence for geological analysis and mineral block modelling, which could potentially reduce exploration timelines from 3-4 months to just 6-7 days.

items.title: Tata Sons board members including Chandrasekaran, Noel Tata to visit Air India HQ for performance review
items.summary: Tata Sons board members will visit Air India headquarters in Gurugram to discuss the airline's performance and strategies. The airline has faced challenges including rising fuel costs and operational issues. Air India's MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam will present on the airline's transformation efforts. Noel Tata has expressed concerns regarding Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman amidst these challenges.

items.title: JPMorgan seeks to revive stalled software debt sale with steep price cuts
items.summary: Banks turn to high-yield bond market to clear $2bn in ‘hung’ debt at double-digit yield

items.title: India-New Zealand FTA to cut wine tariffs from 150% to 25-50% over 10 years
items.summary: India will gradually lower wine tariffs on New Zealand imports, which currently stand at 150%. This reduction is part of the new India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, expected to last for ten years. New Zealand companies are optimistic about expanding their market presence in India. Both countries anticipate mutual benefits from this trade deal in various sectors. An increase in wine consumption in India may follow these tariff reductions.

items.title: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
items.summary: Continued inflation above the Fed's 2% target is pushing central bank officials into a more aggressive stance.

items.title: India on track to hit $1 trillion exports target in FY27: Commerce Secretary
items.summary: India's exports increased by 16.6% in the first half of this fiscal year. The country aims to reach $1 trillion in exports by 2026-27. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal stated that India is on track to meet this goal. Despite global trade uncertainties, India continues to be viewed positively as a trusted trading partner. India achieved record exports of $863 billion in the previous fiscal year.

items.title: Ahmedabad crash: Final investigation report likely soon, Centre tells Supreme Court
items.summary: The investigation into the Air India crash in Ahmedabad that occurred in June 2025 is nearing completion. The Solicitor General has requested a brief adjournment of the court proceedings of two to three weeks. An independent investigation has been sought by the families of the victims and an NGO. The final report will be submitted in a sealed cover, following international protocols.

items.title: Typical energy bill forecast to go up by £443 a year from January as inflation rate rises again
items.summary: Energy bills are expected to jump by 26% a year for a typical household as UK inflation hits its highest rate for a year.

items.title: Heating bills, chocolate and cat food: What the inflation figures mean for you
items.summary: Prices are rising at their fastest pace for a year in the UK, and higher energy costs are on the way.

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin unite $1.48 Trillion military might at Shenzhen: Will nukes be on the table? Why it matters
items.summary: US President Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, ahead of an high stakes meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday.

items.title: RBI warns Yes Bank AT1 bond ruling could weaken future bank rescue framework
items.summary: The case relates to Yes Bank's rescue in 2020, when authorities wrote off Rs 8,415 crore worth of additional Tier-1 (AT1) bonds. These securities are designed to absorb losses when banks face financial distress.

items.title: Trump arrives in China for historic meeting with Xi, Putin
items.summary: President Donald Trump in Shenzhen for historic trilateral talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.

items.title: India, US close to finalising trade deal talks, signing may take time
items.summary: The trade deal negotiations between India and the US are nearing completion, according to Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal. He stated that the legal texts are almost finalized. However, the signing hinges on the establishment of new US tariff rules and the resolution of ongoing Section 301 investigations.

items.title: Lord’s Mark Industries reports ₹82 Crore H1 profit; plans AI healthcare product launches in 2027
items.summary: Lord's Mark Industries Ltd has reported a consolidated net profit of ₹82.01 crore during the first half of FY27, with revenue hitting ₹718.77 crore, outpacing last year's figures. The company is gearing up to introduce innovative products, such as AI-powered dialysis machines and Sickle Cell screening by early 2027, while also pursuing expansion in the US, UK, and Caribbean markets, highlighting a promising growth outlook.

items.title: Govt to charge bulk Scotch imports 162.5% duty and tax amid UK pact standoff
items.summary: India has implemented a hefty 162.5% duty on bulk Scotch imports, surpassing previously established tariffs. This action follows a trade agreement with the UK that aimed to reduce Scotch tariffs to 75%. Investigators claim that Scotch imports are being misclassified, resulting in higher taxes on these goods. Major companies like Pernod Ricard and Diageo are facing disruptions due to blocked shipments at ports.

items.title: RBI may hike interest rates by 75 basis points by Q2 of next year: Goldman Sachs
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is projected to increase interest rates by 75 basis points by the second quarter of 2027. Analysts predict that headline inflation will remain above 6 percent into early 2027 before gradually decreasing. Despite the monetary tightening, India's GDP growth is expected to moderate to 7.2 percent in 2027. Strong domestic demand and an emerging investment cycle are likely to sustain economic activity.

items.title: Investigation into deadly Air India crash in final stage, govt says
items.summary: The Indian government has confirmed that its investigation into the Air India crash is nearing completion. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta presented updates to the Supreme Court, revealing that initial findings point to malfunctioning fuel-control switches as a factor in the engine failure. Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, the captain's father, expressed frustration over assumptions of pilot error. A final report is anticipated to be shared for commentary prior to its release.

items.title: Onion farmers seek measures to ensure Rs 3,000 per quintal amid surplus production outlook
items.summary: Maharashtra onion farmers have asked the Centre to ensure prices of at least Rs 3,000 per quintal by expanding export markets and maintaining a stable export policy, as India is expected to have a sizeable surplus in 2025-26. The growers’ body said better export infrastructure, storage, processing and transparent supply data will be critical to prevent price crashes when market arrivals rise.

items.title: Russia imports record volumes of petrol as Ukraine strikes refineries
items.summary: Shipments a ‘remarkable reversal’ from country’s traditional role as fuel exporter

items.title: Govt planning to expand AB-PMJAY packages for public hospitals from 23 to 112: NHA sources
items.summary: The National Health Authority has proposed expanding health benefit packages reserved for government hospitals under Ayushman Bharat from 23 to 112, adding 89 treatments and procedures. The move aims to improve access to healthcare closer to beneficiaries' homes and channel more reimbursements into strengthening public hospital infrastructure and services.

items.title: IPO-bound Aragen plans to spend Rs 1.5 billion over 2 years for expansion, MD says
items.summary: Aragen Life Sciences intends to invest about 1.5 billion rupees in expanding its drug development and manufacturing operations. The investment is driven by increasing outsourcing demand from global pharmaceutical companies. Aragen plans to enhance its manufacturing capacity for small molecules and biologics over the next two years. The company aims to leverage its customer base to facilitate this growth.

items.title: Security flaw found in Java, world's third-largest programming language
items.summary: The same tech start-up that discovered a PHP flaw used AI to uncover a critical software bug in one of the world's most popular computer language programs.

items.title: Relief for Chanda Kochhar as HC quashes ICICI Bank's nod to prosecute ex-CEO in 'loan fraud' case
items.summary: The Bombay High Court quashed the ICICI Bank's sanction for prosecuting Chanda Kochhar in an alleged fraud case. The court found that the authority granting the sanction did not apply proper judgment to the circumstances. Chanda Kochhar was arrested in December 2022 and received interim bail in January 2023. The case involved a loan of Rs 3,250 crore given to Videocon Group during her tenure.

items.title: Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition, ahead of meeting with Trump and Xi
items.summary: Putin used the speech to emphasize Russia's economic resilience despite U.S. sanctions, and played up opportunities for APEC members in the country.

items.title: China’s Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers ahead of his meeting with Trump and Putin
items.summary: Xi opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen by calling for lower trade and investment barriers, pledging broader access to China’s market and manufacturing sector.

items.title: Indian economic growth seen at annual 7.6% in July-September quarter, economists say
items.summary: India's economy is predicted to grow by 7.6% in the July-September quarter according to economists. Consumer demand has shown resilience, mitigating the effects of rising inflation pressures. Predictions indicate continued strength from passenger vehicle sales and bank credit growth. Despite potential slowdowns in the second half of the fiscal year, investments are expected to improve. The Reserve Bank of India may raise rates as economic conditions evolve.

items.title: Emergency alerts and $75,000 rewards: South Korea fights high-tech exam cheating
items.summary: South Korea moves to crack down on exam cheating with emergency alerts and $75,000 rewards.

items.title: Soybean oil's share rises in India's edible oil import mix
items.summary: India imported 5.83 million tonnes of soybean oil in 2025-26, out of total edible oil imports of 16.92 million tonnes.

items.title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?
items.summary: The former Nvidia chief executive has been at the centre of the artificial intelligence boom.

items.title: China and India mask a growing crisis in global coal
items.summary: Global coal consumption is resilient due to rising demand from China and India, which is increasing despite declining figures elsewhere. However, many coal exporters are struggling financially as they face significant losses in their operations. The coal industry is experiencing tough economic conditions, with job losses and company closures becoming commonplace.

items.title: How India became a rice powerhouse - and why it's becoming a problem
items.summary: India's rice production has significantly increased, bolstered by government subsidies and new crop varieties. This rise in output has led to a surplus that threatens fiscal stability due to high subsidy costs. Political tensions arise between the central and state governments regarding rice pricing and production. While domestic demand is not expected to grow significantly, exports continue to increase.

items.title: Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
items.summary: Nepal has gained authorization to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India amid declining hydropower generation. This approval will remain effective from November 17, 2026, until July 31, 2027. The Nepal Electricity Authority can procure electricity through various transmission lines to meet domestic demand. Several hydropower projects have been affected by recent floods, limiting local production capabilities.

items.title: Jeff Bezos says he was 'heavily involved' in casting Robert Pattinson as new Bond
items.summary: The Amazon chairman says he was originally "biased against" Pattinson "because he's already so famous".

items.title: Adani Airport Holdings unveils next-generation Adani Rewards membership across eight airports
items.summary: Adani Airport Holdings has launched an upgraded rewards membership programme across eight airports, offering passengers benefits worth up to Rs 65,000 annually. Integrated with Adani OneApp, the tier-based scheme combines travel, shopping, dining and lounge privileges as the company looks to boost digital transactions and non-aeronautical revenue.

items.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from all US freeways
items.summary: The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless vehicles from operating on the state's highways following a series of traffic incidents.

items.title: Mukesh Ambani seeks to build satellite capacity for Starlink challenge
items.summary: Reliance Group is eyeing partnerships for manufacturing a 1,600-satellite broadband network aimed at competing with Starlink. The planned low-earth orbit constellation aims for completion by 2035 to enhance connectivity in India. Reliance is negotiating with both domestic and international manufacturers to support its manufacturing goals.

items.title: Nvidia says it won't reinstate Huang as it reports soaring sales
items.summary: The AI chip giant reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday after the dramatic exit of Jensen Huang.

items.title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave
items.summary: Europe hopes to be a leader in a new generation of computer chips which use light to process data.

items.title: As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal
items.summary: China worries the scandal could ramp up pressure on the US to further restrict the sale of advanced chips.
